title: Marcos appoints LTO's Lacanilao as MARINA administrator
summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has appointed Land Transportation Office chief Markus Lacanilao as the new Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA) administrator, Malacañang announced Tuesday.

blocks.text: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has appointed Land Transportation Office chief Markus Lacanilao as the new Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA) administrator, Malacañang announced Tuesday.

"Ang pagtalaga po sa ngayon na si [Undersecretary] Marcos Lacanilao bilang administrator ng MARINA ay isang pagkilala sa kanyang kagalingan," Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said in a press briefing.
(The appointment of Usec Marcos Lacanilao as MARINA administrator today is a recognition of his excellence.)
"Si dating Usec Markus Lacanilao ay nakapag-deliver ng magandang trabaho at magandang mensahe laban sa korapsyon, so mas malaking mission ang iniatang sa kanya ng Pangulo," she added.
(Former Usec Markus Lacanilao has delivered good work and a good message against corruption, so the President has assigned him a bigger mission.)
Lacanilao served as LTO chief since October 2025.
Prior to that, Lacanilao served a Special Envoy on Transnational Crime during the turnover of former president Rodrigo Duterte to the International Criminal Court.
Noreen Bernadette San Luis, a former city administrator of Naga City, will succeed Lacanilao as the new LTO chief.
Meanwhile, Marcos named Presidential Communications Office Undersecretary Jorjette Aquino as the new general manager of the Philippine National Railways.
Castro said Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon will provide more details of the new appointments on Wednesday.
Dizon earlier assured transport group MANIBELA that dismissed LTO personnel, who were involved in corruption would not be allowed to return to the agency.
This came after the transport group gathered outside the LTO Central Office to protest the reported plan to replace LTO Assistant Secretary Lacanilao.
"Over my dead body," Dizon said when asked whether these personnel could return to the agency. — BAP, GMA News
